learning_outcomes.text: Understand the different electronic devices and components most widely used in industrial settings.
Understand the processes involved in the individual manufacturing of integrated circuits, as well as their integration to create a specific active device.
Become familiar with the use of computer tools for circuit simulation, geometric mask editing, and printed circuit board design.
Handle laboratory tools for circuit testing and verification, and printed circuit board manufacturing.

syllabus_topics: The diode: operation and equivalent circuits
MOSFET internal capacitances and high-frequency model
Characteristic parameters of the MOS transistor
Thyristors: diacs, triacs, IGCT, SCR, GTO
Basic aspects of printed circuit board manufacturing
Tutored project based on printed circuit board design
VLSI manufacturing process in CMOS technology
Manufacturing of electronic devices and IC layout

assessment_methods.method: Completion and submission of tasks (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects)

assessment_rules: The final grade consists of a written exam (60%), lab and computer practices (10%), monitoring tasks (15%), and a tutored project (15%). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required on the written exam to pass the course. Unjustified absence in more than one practice session requires passing a non-contributing practice exam. The written exam and tutored project are recoverable in the extraordinary call; practice scores and monitoring task scores are carried over but not recoverable. If the minimum exam or practice requirements are not met, the final grade will be 4.9 if the calculated grade is 5 or higher.
